title: FreeRTOS simulation layer and test framework
summary: A host-side FreeRTOS simulation layer, so RTOS-dependent firmware runs as a normal Linux program on x86 workstations and CI instead of needing the ESP32 target. Test coverage rose from 45% to 80%.
highlights: Simulates tasks, delays, ticks, timers and concurrency in C/C++, with no ESP32 required.
Reused test code from the earlier dual-chip architecture by finding the shared layers, then updating paths, syntax, mocks and flags, instead of writing the suite from scratch.
Added AddressSanitizer, UBSan and Valgrind to the runs; they found real memory leaks and invalid writes before hardware testing.

details.heading: Problem
details.body: The task was a unit test suite for the current single-MCU firmware, whose RTOS-dependent code could only run on the target.

details.heading: My part
details.body: Studied the earlier dual-chip architecture, which had tests, recognised the layers it shared with the current firmware, and built the simulation layer under them.

details.heading: Evidence
details.body: Coverage 45% to 80%. Sanitizer and Valgrind runs found memory leaks and invalid writes.

details.heading: Status
details.body: Professional work. The code is not public.
